name: Isolated Esophageal Duplication Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic mass adjacent to or within the esophageal wall
Histological confirmation of a cyst lined by gastrointestinal epithelium with a smooth muscle coat
Imaging findings consistent with a well-defined, non-communicating cystic lesion on CT or MRI
Symptoms related to esophageal compression such as dysphagia or respiratory distress

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (cyst location, histopathology, and imaging characteristics) must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by histopathological examination after surgical excision.

searchTerms: swallowing problems due to esophageal compression

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cystic mass palpable or visible on imaging adjacent to esophagus
searchTerms: neck cyst palpable or seen on scan

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress or stridor due to airway compression
searchTerms: noisy breathing due to airway blockage

occasional.symptomName: Hematemesis from cyst erosion or ulceration
searchTerms: blood in vomit caused by cyst erosion

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss due to feeding difficulties
searchTerms: poor weight gain due to feeding problems
unintentional weight loss from poor intake

occasional.symptomName: Dysphonia or hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve irritation
searchTerms: voice changes due to throat nerve pressure

occasional.symptomName: Chest wall deformity or scoliosis secondary to mass effect
searchTerms: curved spine due to chest mass
abnormal chest shape caused by tumor
abnormal connection from esophagus to another area
systemic infection due to infected cyst

laboratory: Generally nonspecific; may show signs of infection if cyst is infected
imaging: Well-circumscribed cystic lesion adjacent to esophagus on CT or MRI
Ultrasound may show anechoic cystic structure with characteristic double-layered wall
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; sporadic congenital malformation
other: Histopathology showing cyst lined by gastrointestinal epithelium with smooth muscle coat

distinguishingFeatures: Typically located in mediastinum but not attached to esophagus
Lined by respiratory epithelium rather than gastrointestinal epithelium
Lacks smooth muscle coat surrounding cystic structure
Contains multiple tissue types including fat, calcifications

redFlags: Signs of cyst infection such as fever and sepsis
